---
title: "Architecture"
---

All of the intelligence lives in the Rust core behind a stable websocket protocol.
The browser preview is a thin client, as @fig-architecture shows.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-architecture
%%| fig-cap: "Thin clients talk to the server over a websocket; all rendering lives in the Rust core."
flowchart LR
  BR["Browser preview<br/>(vanilla JS)"]
  subgraph Server["qmd-fast server"]
    direction TB
    WS["Websocket<br/>+ file watcher"]
    subgraph Core["qmd-fast-core"]
      direction TB
      P["Parser<br/>comrak + sourcepos"] --> M["Block model<br/>+ diff"] --> R["Render<br/>html / reveal / book"]
    end
    K["Warm Jupyter kernel"]
  end
  F[(".qmd files")]
  BR <-->|JSON protocol| WS
  WS --> P
  R -->|changed blocks| WS
  F -.->|watch| WS
  M -->|code cells| K --> M
```

| Component | Crate / path | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Core | `crates/core` | Parsing (comrak + sourcepos), the block model, HTML rendering |
| Server | `crates/server` | Websocket dev server, file watcher, Jupyter kernel pool |
| Web client | `web-client/` | Browser preview client (vanilla JS) |

The protocol is open, so an embedded editor client (a VS Code extension, etc.) is
a new thin client, not a rewrite.

## How a save flows

A save flows through the pipeline as @fig-save-flow shows — and crucially, only
the **changed** blocks reach the preview.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-save-flow
%%| fig-cap: "Only the changed blocks are pushed to the preview."
flowchart LR
  save["Save .qmd"] --> watch["File watcher"]
  watch --> parse["Re-parse + block model"]
  parse --> diff["Diff by block id"]
  diff --> ws["Websocket:<br/>changed blocks only"]
  ws --> dom["Preview updates<br/>in place"]
```

The two crates split cleanly: **`qmd-fast-core` does all the thinking and touches
no network** (it parses, models, and renders), while **`qmd-fast-server` is the
long-running process** (CLI, websocket, file watcher, kernel pool). The browser
client is a thin layer that mounts blocks and applies the ops the server sends.

## The codebase map

`crates/core/src` — the library (`qmd-fast-core`):

| Path | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `render/mod.rs` | The render pipeline (`render_internal`) + full-page assembly. The coordinator. |
| `render/emit.rs` | One AST node → HTML (the emitter). |
| `render/divs.rs` | `:::` fenced-div preprocessing + grouping into callouts/columns. |
| `render/figure.rs` | Standalone-image and captioned-cell `<figure>`s. |
| `render/theme.rs` | Theming: light/dark, `.css`/`.scss`, extension themes, the pre-paint script. |
| `render/reveal.rs` | reveal.js slide assembly. |
| `render/extension.rs` | Format extensions + declarative shortcodes. |
| `diff.rs` | Block-level diff (LCS over block ids) → `BlockOp`s. |
| `includes.rs` | `{{< include >}}` resolution + the per-file source map. |
| `math.rs` / `highlight.rs` | Server-side KaTeX / syntect, both offline. |
| `cite.rs` | Citations + cross-references + the CSL/IEEE bibliography. |
| `site/` | Multi-page projects: `config` (`_quarto.yml` model), `book`, `xref` (cross-page refs), `search` (cross-page index), and `mod` (discovery, chrome, page render). |
| `frontmatter.rs` | Front-matter parsing + unknown-key linting. |

`crates/server/src` — the binary (`qmd-fast`):

| Path | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `main.rs` | CLI: the `preview` / `build` / `render` / `blocks` subcommands. |
| `serve.rs` | Single-document websocket server + file watcher. |
| `serve_site.rs` | Multi-page site/book server (per-page state, cross-page nav, hot reload). |
| `exec.rs` | Runs a doc's code cells and splices outputs back as blocks (incremental: the first changed cell + everything downstream). |
| `kernel.rs` | The warm Jupyter kernel (ZMQ), reused across edits, with interrupt + timeout. |
| `log.rs` | Colourised dev-server console output. |

`web-client/` — the browser preview (vanilla JS, no build step): `client.js`
(mounts blocks, applies ops, the dev menu, click-to-source), `search.js` (the
Cmd-K palette), `toc-spy.js` (the scrollspy). The core also ships JS *assets*
(`code-enhance.js` with the `window.qmdEnhancers` registry, `mermaid.js`) that
both the live client and the static build inject.

The next two chapters go deeper: [the rendering pipeline](rendering.qmd) (how a
`.qmd` becomes blocks) and [extending qmd-fast](extending.qmd) (the conventions,
how to add a feature, and the dev workflow).
